After you land

Your first visit to a BMO branch.

This is where your account becomes ready to use. The branch team checks your documents, activates the account and helps with your debit card.

  1. When should I go?

    Aim for your first few days, before you need to use the transferred funds. This is a planning suggestion, not a bank deadline.

  2. Do I need an appointment?

    BMO’s pre-arrival guide says you can walk in. You can also book ahead to plan the visit around your arrival.

  3. What should I bring?

    • The passport used in your application
    • Your immigration documents and BMO welcome letter
    • School registration and expected graduation date for the student Plan

Before you decide

Let’s clear up a few things.

The costs, the timing and the “what ifs” are worth understanding before you apply.

Still have a question?

WhatsApp us

Prefer email?

care@aetherconnect.ai
What is the student offer?
Eligible full-time students can receive a BMO Performance Plan with no monthly Plan fees, including up to one year after graduation. BMO verifies your enrolment and expected graduation date. The Student Practical Plan and Student Performance Plan are different stages of your account journey. Other service and transaction fees can apply.
Are there fees before I arrive?
BMO sets the account’s fees. Eligible full-time students get $0 monthly Plan fees while studying, plus up to a year after graduation, once BMO verifies enrolment. Other service and transaction fees may apply, and your home bank may charge for sending the transfer.
What does the transfer cost?
That depends on the bank you send from. Before you send, ask it for the exchange rate, its fees and the amount expected to arrive in Canadian dollars. Other BMO service and transaction fees may apply.
How much can I send?
Up to CAD 75,000 in one pre-arrival wire, sent in Canadian dollars. Follow the wire instructions BMO gives you for your account.
How long do approval and the transfer take?
BMO offers processing in minutes for eligible countries and applications; some countries or document checks take longer. Transfer times depend on the sending bank, so ask it for an expected arrival date before you send.
What if my study permit is refused?
Contact BMO about your account and about returning the funds. Keep your BMO welcome information and your transfer records, so the bank can help trace the payment.
Can I use the money as soon as I land?
You can use your transferred funds once you’ve activated the account at a BMO branch. Aim to visit in your first few days, and plan separately for any payments due before that visit.
What information does this check need?
Two answers: your country of residence and your study permit status. No passwords, PINs or passport uploads. For the full application that follows, have your passport and school or immigration documents ready.
Does Aether Connect charge anything?
This eligibility check is free. Aether Connect is not a bank: BMO provides the account, makes the decision on your application and sets its fees.
Who holds my money, and is it protected?
BMO does, in your own BMO account, not Aether Connect. Eligible deposits at BMO are covered by CDIC up to CAD 100,000 per depositor, per category, within its coverage conditions.
For parents

A big step for them. A few answers for you.

You want to know where the money goes, who handles it and what happens if plans change. Those are sensible questions to ask.

  • Where is the money held?

    In your child’s BMO account, not with Aether Connect. Eligible deposits have CDIC protection within its coverage limits.

  • Can a parent send the funds?

    Use the student’s BMO wire instructions. Before sending, ask BMO whether the transfer can come from a parent’s account and which sender details are required.

  • What if the plans change?

    Contact BMO about a delayed arrival or returning the funds. Keep the welcome information and transfer records so the bank can help you trace the payment.

It helps to talk it through together.
